questions.q: What happened to the Indian textile industry when cheap British cloth arrived?
questions.a: The Indian textile industry, once one of the most advanced, was destroyed. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks it grew or stayed the same, indicating they don't understand the concept of "competition" between handmade and factory goods.

questions.q: Why did British policies force farmers to grow crops like indigo instead of food crops?
questions.a: They were forced to grow "cash crops" to supply raw materials for British industries. If a student says "to feed more people," they are missing the point that the British prioritized their own industrial profit over the food security of the local population.

questions.q: If a farmer is forced to grow indigo instead of rice, what happens to their local village?
questions.a: 1. Identify the shift: Food crop (rice) to cash crop (indigo). 2. Identify the consequence: Less food available. 3. Conclude: Famines or food shortages occur because the village can no longer feed itself. A wrong answer shows a failure to link agricultural choices to food security.

questions.q: Compare the position of an Indian weaver before and after the influx of British machine-made cloth.
questions.a: Before, they were skilled independent producers; after, they lost their livelihood because they could not compete with the low cost of mass-produced British cloth. If the student focuses only on "cheaper clothes," they fail to analyze the impact on the artisan's life.

questions.q: Was the British economic policy beneficial to the Indian common person? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, because it prioritized British industrial wealth at the expense of local manufacturing and food security. A wrong answer suggests the student is being influenced by myths of "progress" without looking at the cost to the actual population.

questions.q: Create a scenario showing how a local market would look before and after the arrival of British goods.
questions.a: A good answer describes a vibrant bazaar of local crafts before, and a market dominated by uniform British imports after. Poor answers will just list random items without showing the change in the source or the economic shift.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The British Raj refers to the period of direct rule by the British Crown over the Indian subcontinent, which ______ changed India’s economy by prioritizing British industrial needs over local production.
Fill in the blank: Imagine your family makes beautiful ______ sweaters that are famous in the whole city.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to describe how British policies turned India from a manufacturer into a supplier of raw materials and explain one negative impact on Indian farmers or weavers.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Imagine your family makes ______ handmade sweaters that are famous in the whole city.
